questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make new friends in a big city
Why people choose to live on islands
Loneliness, and whether it is a new idea
The history of the English novel
questions.why: Neil says they'll explore whether loneliness is a new idea or something humans have always experienced.

questions.q: What example of loneliness does Rob give?
options: Moving to a new country
Feeling you don't fit in somewhere
Working from home every day
Losing a pet
questions.why: Rob says you might feel lonely because friends go out without you or because you don't fit in.

questions.q: What has research found about long periods of social isolation?
options: They help people become more creative
They only affect older people
They mostly harm physical health
They are bad for us, especially mentally
questions.why: Rob says research has found prolonged social isolation is bad for us, particularly mentally.

questions.q: What does Fay Bound Alberti say about Robinson Crusoe?
options: It never mentions loneliness
It is the loneliest novel ever written
It was written in the 19th century
It is about a woman looking for love
questions.why: She says in an 18th-century novel like Robinson Crusoe there's not a single reference to loneliness.

questions.q: According to Fay, what were many women in Victorian novels searching for?
options: Solitude so they could write
Work outside the home
A partner, to feel complete and happy
Adventure on desert islands
questions.why: She says Victorian fiction is full of women in search of 'the significant other' to find happiness.

questions.q: Why did writers like Virginia Woolf look for solitude?
options: It helped them be creative
They disliked other writers
They were ill and needed rest
Their families sent them away
questions.why: Rob says some female authors looked for solitude because it helped them be creative.

questions.q: According to Fay, when does loneliness become a real problem?
options: When it happens after a wedding
When it affects young people
When it happens more than once
When it becomes long-lasting
questions.why: She says pinch points cause temporary loneliness, and it's a problem when it becomes chronic.

questions.q: Why does Neil suggest checking in with friends and family?
options: It stops people from feeling bored at home
Others can't always see that someone is lonely
It is polite to call everyone at least once a week
It helps you get over a painful break-up faster
questions.why: Neil says loneliness isn't always obvious, so it's good to ask people if they're OK.
